title: Restrictions
raw_text:
9/30/26, 5:12 AM

e The next customer enters the premise on the same day: 2023-02-25 at 16:30; the corresponding utilities contract 2 has the
move-in date: 2023-02-26.

Restrictions
The following restrictions exist:

e The exact move-in time must either be found on the move-in date or on the day before the move-in.

e The move-out time must be found on the move-out date.

Different restrictions to those described above apply to the Japanese market. In this case, the logic is dependent on the billing
period applied. For more details, please see Handling the Exact Move-In and Move-Out Time for the Japanese Billing Period.

The move-in and move-out time can be displayed and changed in the transactions Display Contract (ES22) and Change
Contract (ES21) on the tab “Page 3” in the section “Alternative Activation” in the fields start date / start time and end date /
end time. You always maintain the date and time; the system automatically observes the time zone of the installation. The checks

applied in the transactions are very basic. For example, an inconsistency that is caused by a possible overlap of two subsequent
utilities contracts (example: end date 1 = start date 2; end time 1> start time 2), is not checked.

If the consumption at the utilities installation is measured as a time series using a smart meter, the move-in and move-out time
can be considered in TOU and RTP billing to calculate the consumption accurately from the start and to the end of the service. For
more technical details, please see SAP Note 3394464 ve.

Connection Object

Definition
A connection object is usually a building but can also be a piece of property or a facility, such as a fountain or construction site.

Since an address is allocated to a connection object, the connection object links premises, device locations and connections to the
postal regional structure.

Integration

The connection object is a functional location from the Plant Maintenance (PM) application component. Therefore, maintenance
is managed using the functions of the Service Management (PM-SMA) component, for example, if you wish to organize the repair

and maintenance of devices at the connection object level. Maintenance and repairs are billed using the Sales and Distribution
(SD) application component.

Other Information

For each connection object you can define any number of static notes. These can be printed on meter reading orders, for example,
to give field service employees extra information. Example include "Ring Mr Y’s doorbell," "Beware of the dog," and so on. You can
also use the dynamic notes predefined in the system (for example "Installation blocked for meter reading,” "Meter reading already
entered.")
